title: Model admission API: publish service-level profiles and version-lock hints
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Add a new concise "Model Admission API" endpoint to make first-class service-level capability and performance profiles available to API consumers and runtime routers, and to publish version-locking hints for safe pinning. This is intended to replace ad-hoc discovery via model manifest scraping and provide a stable, typed contract for:

1) ServiceProfile (what the runtime and platform should advertise):
   - id: canonical model id (string)
   - advertised_versions: list of versions with stability tags and deprecation timeline (string[] described in docs)
   - recommended_version_hints: order-of-preference strings for pinning and fallback routing
   - max_context_tokens: integer (safe guidance for allocation and batching)
   - typical_context_distribution: high-level bucketed guidance (short|medium|long) for kernel selection
   - preferred_batch_sizes: list of integers (suggested batch sizes to hit efficiency sweet spots)
   - latency_slo_ms: percentiles and targets (P50/P95 indicated via documented string format)
   - cost_units_per_token: normalized cost guidance for router optimizations
   - supported_features: strings, e.g., streaming, tool_calling, structured_output, kv_cache_affinity
   - attention_behavior: free-text guidance when special kernel paths are required

2) AdmissionHints (routing + pinning helpers):
   - lock_affinity_tags: short strings used by Dedicated/Private to opt into compatible runtime builds
   - incompatibilities: explicit feature flags that mark known runtime incompatibilities with older kernels
   - fallback_chain: ordered version ids to use when pinned version is unavailable

Implementation notes and goals:
- Expose a new endpoint GET /v1/models/{model_id}/admission that returns the ServiceProfile and AdmissionHints. The payload is intentionally normative text-heavy to avoid brittle version coupling; numeric fields are normalized to strings in the API contract for forward compatibility.
- Backwards compatibility: existing manifest and profile endpoints continue to operate. The new contract is additive and targetted to router logic and onboarding flows.
- Runtime integration: routing service will consult recommended_version_hints + lock_affinity_tags to decide: a) whether the request can be served by a cheaper/quantized variant, b) whether to respect customer-specified pinning or transition to a safe fallback.
- Security & compliance: sensitive internal telemetry is not exposed in the public contract. The API surface contains only high-level performance guidance; KMS/usage-based metrics remain in internal telemetry endpoints.

Open trade-offs and decisions:
- Schema strictness vs flexibility: prefer a small set of well-documented string fields rather than a deeply nested typed schema to avoid frequent version churn when we add experimental kernels.
- Numerics as strings: allows us to evolve units (tokens vs subtokens) without immediate API churn; router will parse and validate in a best-effort way.
- Pin semantics: we provide hints, not hard enforcement. Customers can pin specific versions via existing model pin APIs; admission endpoints will surface recommended and fallback sequences.

Migration & rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal): expose endpoint for a small set of curated models (open and internal Canary builds). Runtime and router teams toggle-on reading hints for non-customer-facing routing only.
- Phase 2 (soft public): publish the endpoint for all hosted models with the console flag to display profiles. SDKs will add a v1 helper to fetch and interpret the admission profile.
- Phase 3 (enforceable tooling): provide console validations and warnings when customers pin to versions flagged with deprecation timelines.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for serialization and tolerant parsing of numeric-as-string fields.
- Integration tests: router behavior change when preferred_batch_sizes and fallback_chain are present.
- Load test: ensure the new endpoint can handle spikes (cached) and that routers degrade gracefully when admission endpoint is unavailable.

Success criteria:
- Router uses admission hints for at least one cost-optimization (quantized fallback) in production and demonstrates >=10% token cost reduction for the selected workload without regressing P95 latency beyond agreed SLO.
- Console surfaces profiles for >=80% of onboarded models within two release cycles.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.example.com/confluence/model-admission-api-design
- API spec draft (OpenAPI excerpt): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/215
